tools.name: kayako_get_me
tools.description: Fetch the Kayako user these credentials belong to (name, role, teams, locale). A cheap way to confirm the subdomain and credentials work. Kayako: GET /api/v1/me.json.

tools.name: kayako_list_cases
tools.description: List cases (conversations / tickets), newest-updated first. Filter by status type, tags, max priority level, or a requester identity (email, Twitter screen name, Facebook username, phone); or fetch specific ids. Nested resources are references unless `include` expands them. Kayako: GET /api/v1/cases

tools.name: kayako_get_case
tools.description: Fetch one case (conversation) by id: subject, requester, assignee, status, priority, type, SLA metrics, custom fields, last post preview. Use include (e.g. 'user,case_status,case_priority,team') to expand references and fields='+tags' for tags. Kayako: GET /api/v1/cases/{id}.json.

tools.name: kayako_list_case_posts
tools.description: Read a case's timeline: customer messages, agent replies and internal notes (newest first). By default activities are excluded; filters='NOTES' for internal notes only, 'MESSAGES' for messages, 'ALL' to include activities. Paginate with before_id / after_id (one at a time). Kayako: GET /api/v1/cases

tools.name: kayako_list_channels
tools.description: List the channels (MAIL mailbox, TWITTER, FACEBOOK, NOTE) usable for a reply on an existing case (pass case_id) or for a new case (omit case_id; optionally pass the requester's user_id). A channel's account.id is the channel_id to pass to kayako_reply_to_case / kayako_create_case. Kayako: GET /api/v

tools.name: kayako_list_case_options
tools.description: List the instance's case statuses (id, label, type), priorities (id, label, level) or types (id, label, type) — the ids needed for status_id / priority_id / type_id when creating, updating or replying to a case. Kayako: GET /api/v1/cases/{statuses|priorities|types}.json.

tools.name: kayako_search
tools.description: Unified search across conversations (cases), users and organizations. Returns id, title, snippet, relevance and resource type; pass fields='*' to get each full resource inline. Max 30 results. Kayako: GET /api/v1/search.json.

tools.name: kayako_list_users
tools.description: List users (customers, collaborators, agents, admins), newest first, optionally by role type or specific ids. To find a user by email or name use kayako_search. Kayako: GET /api/v1/users.json.

tools.name: kayako_get_user
tools.description: Fetch one user by id: name, role, organization, teams, identities (emails, phones, social), custom fields. include='identity_email,organization' expands references. Kayako: GET /api/v1/users/{id}.json.

tools.name: kayako_list_organizations
tools.description: List customer organizations (name, domains, phone, custom fields), oldest first. To find one by name use kayako_search with resources=['ORGANIZATIONS']. Kayako: GET /api/v1/organizations.json.

tools.name: kayako_list_organization_cases
tools.description: List the cases (conversations) raised by members of one organization, newest-updated first. Kayako: GET /api/v1/organizations/{id}/cases.json.

tools.name: kayako_list_teams
tools.description: List agent teams (id, title, member count) — the ids for assigned_team_id. Kayako: GET /api/v1/teams.json.

tools.name: kayako_list_roles
tools.description: List user roles (id, title, type OWNER/ADMIN/AGENT/COLLABORATOR/CUSTOMER) — the role_id needed by kayako_create_user. Kayako: GET /api/v1/roles.json.

tools.name: kayako_list_articles
tools.description: List knowledge-base articles, optionally by section, tags, or PUBLISHED / PINNED. Titles and contents are locale references unless include='locale_field'. Kayako: GET /api/v1/articles.json.

tools.name: kayako_get_article
tools.description: Fetch one knowledge-base article with its localized titles and contents expanded (include defaults to 'locale_field'), status, section, tags, votes and help-center URL. Kayako: GET /api/v1/articles/{id}.json.

tools.name: kayako_search_help_center
tools.description: Search the help center's articles and/or public conversations. Returns references (e.g. {id, resource_type: 'article'}); read an article with kayako_get_article. Kayako: GET /api/v1/helpcenter/search.json.

tools.name: kayako_create_case
tools.description: WRITE: open a new case (conversation) for a requester. channel MAIL sends the first message to the customer by email from the mailbox given as channel_id; channel NOTE creates it with an internal note and emails nobody. Get channel ids from kayako_list_channels and status/priority/type ids from kaya

tools.name: kayako_update_case
tools.description: WRITE: change a case's subject, requester, assignee (team/agent), status, priority, type, brand, form, tags or custom fields. Sends nothing to the customer. `tags` sets the case's tag list (use kayako_add_case_tags to append). Trashing is deliberately not exposed. Kayako: PUT /api/v1/cases/{id}.json

tools.name: kayako_reply_to_case
tools.description: WRITE: add a post to a case. channel NOTE adds an INTERNAL note visible only to agents (no channel_id needed). channel MAIL/TWITTER/FACEBOOK sends a PUBLIC reply to the customer — get channel_id from kayako_list_channels with case_id. Can also set status/priority/assignee in the same call. Kayako: P

tools.name: kayako_add_case_tags
tools.description: WRITE: add tags to a case, keeping its existing tags. Kayako: POST /api/v1/cases/{id}/tags.json.

tools.name: kayako_create_user
tools.description: WRITE: create a user — typically a CUSTOMER to use as requester_id on a new case. role_id comes from kayako_list_roles. Collaborator/agent/admin roles also require email and team_ids. No password is set by this tool. Kayako: POST /api/v1/users.json.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "kayako_get_me" references sensitive artifacts (credentials). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: kayako_list_cases, kayako_get_case, kayako_list_case_posts, kayako_list_users, kayako_get_user, kayako_get_article, kayako_create_case, kayako_reply_to_case · Private data: kayako_get_me, kayako_create_user · Public sink: kayako_list_cases, kayako_get_case, kayako_list_users, kayako_create_case, kayako_reply_to_case, kayako_add_case_tags, kayako_create_user.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: kayako_list_cases, kayako_get_case, kayako_list_case_posts, kayako_list_users, kayako_get_user, kayako_get_article, kayako_create_case, kayako_reply_to_case · Private data: kayako_get_me, kayako_create_user · Public sink: kayako_list_cases, kayako_get_case, kayako_list_users, kayako_create_case, kayako_reply_to_case, kayako_add_case_tags, kayako_create_user

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
